content:
We need to propose a retrosynthesis route with 3 reactions for target SMILES: Cc1ccc(NS(=O)(=O)c2ccc(/C=C/C(=O)Nc3ccccc3N)cc2)cc1.

The guidance: three steps: 1) sulfonamide formation (sulfonyl chloride + amine). 2) Doebner modification to form the α,β-unsaturated carboxylic acid (the C=C-COOH part). 3) amide formation (carboxylic acid + amine coupling).

Thus retrosynthetic direction: target -> break amide bond to give acid and aniline (or amine). Then break the α,β-unsaturated acid to give aldehyde + malonic acid? Actually Doebner modification: aromatic aldehyde + malonic acid -> α,β-unsaturated acid. So retro: the unsaturated acid fragment (C=C-CO-NH-Ph) is formed from aromatic aldehyde (maybe 4-formyl phenyl) and malonic acid, then decarboxylation yields the unsaturated acid. In our target, the unsaturated acid is attached to aromatic ring via C=C to carbonyl amide. The fragment is /C=C/C(=O)N-PhNH2? Actually structure: ...c2ccc(/C=C/C(=O)Nc3ccccc3N)cc2. So we have a phenyl ring (ring B) bearing a side chain: trans-CH=CH-CO-NH-Ph-NH2 (an aniline). So the side chain is cinnamoyl amide attached to an aniline.

Thus retrosynthesis: Step 1: amide formation between cinnamic acid (trans-CH=CH-COOH) and aniline (c3ccccc3N). So break amide to give cinnamic acid and aniline.

Step 2: cinnamic acid from Doebner modification: aromatic aldehyde (p-methyl? Actually the aldehyde is attached to the phenyl ring B at the position where side chain attaches). The aldehyde is p-methyl? The phenyl B has a methyl? No, the phenyl B is unsubstituted except the side chain. So aldehyde is p-formyl phenyl (i.e., 4-formyl phenyl). So break C=C double bond formation: retro Doebner: cinnamic acid from 4-formyl phenyl (p-formyl phenyl) + malonic acid.

Step 3: sulfonamide formation: The sulfonyl chloride (p-tolyl sulfonyl chloride) + aniline (the first phenyl A with methyl). Actually target has sulfonamide linking phenyl A (p-tolyl) to phenyl B (the sulfonyl attached to phenyl B). So break sulfonamide to give p-tolyl sulfonyl chloride and aniline (phenyl B with side chain). So the aniline is the phenyl B bearing the side chain (cinnamoyl amide). So after step 2 we have phenyl B with side chain (cinnamic acid amide). That is the same as the aniline after amide formation? Wait: after step 1 we have phenyl B with side chain as cinnamic acid (not amide). Actually step 1 amide formation: product is target. Retro: break amide to give cinnamic acid attached to phenyl B (still attached to phenyl B) and aniline (c3ccccc3N). So the phenyl B after step 1 is still attached to sulfonyl group? Yes, the sulfonamide is between phenyl A and phenyl B. So after step 1, we have phenyl B bearing sulfonamide (connected to phenyl A) and side chain as cinnamic acid (instead of amide). So step 2: break the C=C double bond formation to give aldehyde on phenyl B (p-formyl phenyl) and malonic acid. The sulfonamide remains.

Step 3: break sulfonamide to give p-tolyl sulfonyl chloride and phenyl B (now aldehyde). So final precursors: p-tolyl sulfonyl chloride, malonic acid, and aniline (c3ccccc3N). Also need maybe a coupling agent for amide formation later.

Thus we need to produce a JSON route with three reaction nodes.

We need template IDs for each step. We have some templates from search results. For amide formation (carboxylic acid + amine) we have template ID 401931 (retro_smarts shows amide formation). That template corresponds to breaking amide to give acid and amine? The retro template is [#7:2]-[C;...]=O/[CH]=[C]>> ... Actually the retro template shows amide to acid + alkene? Wait: The retro_smarts_template: '[#7:2]-[C;H0;D3;+0:1](=[O;D1;H0:3])/[CH;D2;+0:4]=[C:5]>>C-C(-C)(-C)-O-[C;H0;D3;+0:1](-[#7:2])=[O;D1;H0:3].O-C(=O)-[CH;D2;+0:4]=[C:5]'. This seems to be a retro of amide formation plus maybe protecting group? But the canonical forward is amide formation from acid and alkene? Actually the forward (canonical) is C-C(-C)(-C)-O-[C...]=O .O-C(=O)-[CH]=[C]>> amide. That seems to be amide formation from acid and amine? Not sure.

But we can use this template ID 401931 for step 1 (amide formation). We'll need to verify matching.

We also need a template for Doebner modification (aldehyde + malonic acid -> α,β-unsaturated acid). Search for functional groups broken: "C-C double bonds" formed, "aldehydes" broken? Let's search.
